FFmpeg source and binary identification (verification record; not a compliance approval)

The Windows Electron distribution includes ffmpeg.dll as a separate file. Chromium's LICENSES.chromium.html identifies FFmpeg primarily under LGPL v2.1 or later, with separately licensed components.

Electron: 45.0.0; Chromium: 156.0.8078.48
Chromium FFmpeg source repository: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/third_party/ffmpeg.git

PE export table inspection found 53 FFmpeg API functions, including av_read_frame, avcodec_find_decoder, and avformat_open_input. The exports do not include av_version_info or avcodec_configuration, so configuration could not be queried through those API functions. Electron v45.0.0 build/args/release.gn sets is_component_ffmpeg=true and describes a shared FFmpeg library for LGPL dynamic linking. Electron's build/args/ffmpeg.gn is for the standalone ffmpeg.zip artifact and sets proprietary_codecs=false; it does not establish the effective configuration of this app's ffmpeg.dll. Effective flags, external libraries, exact source-to-binary rebuild correspondence, DLL replacement/relaunch, and public download placement remain unverified. Do not treat this record or archive as proof of compliance.

Official project guidance: https://ffmpeg.org/legal.html
